leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members put optical lattice clocks, credited to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye, as their single preferred prize part. They share the same two names, the same core argument (magic-wavelength trapping, reproduction at the 1e-18 level in several laboratories and species, clean attribution) and the same main reservation (overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-trapping prizes, and the redefinition of the second not yet having happened). Their citations differ in emphasis: Johansson and Kroll stress development and the 10^-18 level, Lindroth stresses invention and realisation, Olsson and Pearce write invention and realisation with Katori's proposal and Ye's accuracy work in distinct roles. Two of the five (Johansson and Pearce, by their own statements) moved toward this position after reading the opening results, so it should be read as an alignment around the lowest-dispute attribution rather than as unanimous enthusiasm for a new discovery. The five statements do not settle priority between Katori and Ye's group or the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto and others.

One member (Danielsson) prefers IceCube and high-energy astrophysical neutrinos as a single part, with Francis Halzen and Albrecht Karle only; the shortlist entry also lists Shigeru Yoshida, and Danielsson asks the experts whether Yoshida's analysis leadership is comparable to Karle's construction role. His case is that this is a discovery in the plainest sense, confirmed through several IceCube channels. His own reservations are attribution across AMANDA and IceCube, the absence of a comparably sensitive second telescope, and thin opening support. Other members refer to B010 as an alternative or a taste (Olsson and Pearce list it among alternatives, Lindroth lists it second alternative), but none of them prefers it in the round-1 configuration.

One member (Eriksson) prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with Allan MacDonald, Rafi Bistritzer and Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, as a theory-plus-experiment prediction confirmed by independent groups. He accepts that the pairing mechanism is unsettled, that the field may be young, and that Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers is not among the credited names. His proximity to the field is noted by him as a possible bias.

One member (Mehlig) prefers the theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting and the hexatic phase (Halperin, Nelson, Young) as a simple universal mechanism with clear three-person attribution. He states that no other colleague ranked it, that the 2016 topological-phase-transition prize may be seen as covering the defect idea, and that experimental maturity of the hexatic phase varies by system. This is a minority position grounded in theory and mechanism, not in measurement or technology impact.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 files name a single-part prize (one ballot ID) as the preferred configuration, and none combines two shortlist entries in one prize.
Attribution is treated by every member as a decisive practical test. Members who prefer B043, B010, B029 or B020 all state their own attribution weakness in their case against.

Every member who responds to B043 accepts that Katori and Ye's lattice-clock results have been reproduced independently in several laboratories and species, and that the credit is cleaner than for most other shortlisted entries.
Everyone who mentions it recognises the same B043 weakness: overlap with the 2005 (Hall, Hansch) and 2012 (Wineland, Haroche) prizes and the pending redefinition of the second.
No member prefers circuit QED (B023) in round 1. Johansson, whose opening first choice was B023, names it only as an alternative, and he has disclosed that he should recuse on it.
Several members request outside expert advice on early history (IceCube credit, lattice-clock priority) before any final decision.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks (B043) count as a new discovery or invention, or as a very successful refinement of precision timekeeping. Lindroth reads them as a discovery about what a quantum system can do; Danielsson, in ranking IceCube first, regards B043 as mature and well confirmed but hesitates that no new phenomenon was found; Pearce notes that a clock result is a window on the universe less directly than neutrino astronomy.

Whether the diffuse high-energy neutrino flux (B010) is itself the discovery, independently established within IceCube analyses, or whether the lack of a second telescope at comparable sensitivity (KM3NeT, Baikal-GVD) and the few-sigma level of individual source associations weaken the case. Danielsson and Pearce, in the same exchange, treat the diffuse flux as the first chapter and the source associations as the second.
Whether the pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (B029) must be understood before recognition, or whether flat-band correlated phases suffice.

Whether two-dimensional melting (B020) is already covered by the 2016 topological-phase-transition prize, and whether its first-order versus continuous character in specific systems weakens a citation.
attribution_disputes: B043 credits Katori and Ye only. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all state that Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hollberg, Hinkley or other lineages are left out, and Kroll and Olsson explicitly ask for the early priority record to be checked. Olsson asks whether a narrow citation suffices or the pair should be broadened, since Takamoto and others realised the first lattice clock with Katori. Ye's scope across combs, clocks and molecules makes the citation delicate.

B010 as listed on the shortlist has three names (Halzen, Karle, Yoshida), while Danielsson's configuration names two (Halzen and Karle). Kroll's file is cited by Danielsson as listing Yoshida as a third name. How credit divides among Halzen, Karle, Yoshida and the AMANDA pioneers is unresolved, and members ask for expert advice.

B029 omits Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experimental papers, and the wider moire community (Dean, Kim, Yacoby and others) has claims. Mehlig also asks whether a 2011 theory plus 2018 experiment pairing is enough.
B020 (Halperin, Nelson, Young) is described by its sole supporter as having clear three-person attribution, which no other member contests in the files.
maturity_disputes: B043: whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the second, or whether the 10^-18 level, reproduced for about twenty years, already makes the invention mature enough. Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all raise this in some form.
B010: whether independent confirmation from KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD, or improved IceCube source statistics, would change the case for waiting a year, as Danielsson asks.
B029: whether a few more years of consolidation are needed given early sample variability and the unsettled pairing mechanism.
B020: the work is old, and Mehlig says the committee may ask why it was not recognised earlier, but he also argues that the authors should be honoured while they can be.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs WACQT and works at Chalmers MC2 in superconducting circuits, and says he should recuse on circuit QED (B023) and probably on B015 and B003. He reports no connection to Katori or Ye, so no recusal is needed for B043.

Kroll notes institutional overlap with Johansson through the WACQT leadership team (relevant to B023), and says he would recuse on any configuration involving quantum memories or rare-earth crystals, none of which is on the shortlist.
Eriksson is a theoretical condensed-matter physicist whose field is close to B029, and notes this as possible bias; no collaboration with MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero.
Pearce (chair) is an astroparticle experimentalist in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, which may bias him toward IceCube (B010); he has no apparent connection to the IceCube or lattice-clock groups.
Danielsson notes that his profile does not say whether Uppsala colleagues take part in IceCube, and would disclose it if so.

Lindroth is a close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) but no shortlisted candidate is a collaborator; Olsson and Mehlig mention shared Chalmers or Gothenburg affiliation with Johansson. Neither reports a recusal need.
questions_for_round2: Should B043 be cited for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, for the development of lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, or more narrowly for the magic-wavelength concept, and does that wording separate it clearly from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-trapping prizes?

Does the primary literature support Katori and Ye as the decisive pair for B043, and do the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hollberg, Hinkley or others require a wider or different set of laureates? Which expert reviewer can settle priority?
Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second before recognising lattice clocks, and which members regard it as a necessary condition and which as only a confirming milestone?
For B010, should the laureate set be Halzen and Karle only, or include Yoshida, and what do experts say about the roles of AMANDA pioneers and of analysis leaders in the diffuse-flux discovery?

What independent evidence exists, from KM3NeT, Baikal-GVD or improved IceCube analyses, that would change the maturity assessment of B010, and would Danielsson or others make B010 a preferred configuration if it were available?
For B029, how should the committee treat the absence of Yuan Cao, and is an unresolved pairing mechanism a barrier to recognition this year?

Can supporters of B020 (Mehlig) and B029 (Eriksson) state what evidence would move them to B043 or another configuration, and can B043 supporters say whether they would join a different configuration if the expert reports disfavour a two-person clock prize?
Should the committee allow a two-part prize in round 2, pairing B043 with another achievement, or retain a single-part prize, given that no member currently prefers a combined configuration?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows five of eight members preferring B043 as a single two-laureate prize, with one member each preferring B010, B029 and B020. The B043 group converged largely because its attribution is the least disputed, and its members acknowledge the novelty and redefinition questions. The minority positions are each substantive and are held for different reasons: discovery character (B010), prediction confirmed by experiment (B029) and theoretical mechanism (B020). Round 2 should focus on the priority record for B043, the wording against earlier precision-metrology prizes, and what expert evidence would change any minority member's preferred configuration. I express no committee ruling here and I disclose that my own earlier taste leaned toward IceCube.
